properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony, 2026-09-23, at the dev_reflow2 hub, about hxm_program (his work hub over the HXM beamline repos): "For hxm_program, the codegraph stuff was my initial attempt at creating a hub. Later, I created reflow2 and adopted that into the hxm_program repo. As I'm still developing reflow2, only I'm using that in the hxm_program and others are using the codegraph. That being said, the codegraph is a json file if I remember right and the reflow2 design is a json file. Could the codegraph become the reflow2 graph? Then only one json is maintained?"

═══ WHAT THE TWO FILES ACTUALLY ARE (read 2026-09-23, hxm_program at ab6e80c) ═══
· codegraphs/<repo>/graph.json: GRAPHIFY output, one per upstream repo (nine: the three profile collections, hextools/pdftools/xpdtools, pdfstream, nslsii, hex-acq-pyepics). DESCRIPTIVE and GENERATED: nodes are files, functions and classes from the AST (`_origin: "ast"`) plus "rationale" nodes; links are contains/calls/imports/inherits/references/rationale_for, with a confidence. hextools alone is 130 nodes and 192 links. Stamped `built_at_commit`, rebuilt by codegraphs/build.sh, and AGENTS.md forbids hand-editing it. Colleagues use it (plus its HTML view) because they do not use reflow2.
· reflow2.json: the NORMATIVE design, one for the whole program (451 nodes: 83 decisions, 33 requirements, 40 capabilities, 15 components, 41 artifacts). Hand-kept through an agent, and holds WHY.
So they are graphs at different altitudes: one says what the code IS, the other what it is FOR.

═══ OPTIONS, in Anthony's words where he gave them (none chosen) ═══
(a) ONE FILE, LITERALLY: import each codegraph into the design as nodes, so reflow2.json holds the code map too.
(b) ONE MAINTAINED, ONE DERIVED: the design is the only file anyone maintains. The code map is regenerated on demand (graphify, or a reflow2 view) and never stored as design content. Read that way, "only one json is maintained" is ALREADY TRUE of the codegraph, because it is generated, not maintained. Its real cost is regeneration and staleness ("freshen" in AGENTS.md), not hand upkeep.
(c) LINK, DON'T MERGE: register each graph.json as an Artifact with its checksum, so reconcile says when it is stale against its repo. Let design Components and Artifacts point at codegraph node ids, so "show me the code behind this capability" is a lookup. Two files, each with one job, joined by references.
(d) USE THE CODEGRAPH AS ADOPT'S MECHANICAL HALF: feed graphify's file and function inventory into adopt as the deterministic structural pass (artifacts and their hashes, plus cycles as findings), and spend the model only on intent. This is dec:idea-mechanical-code-structure-ingest's "narrower version", with an existing extractor instead of a new one, and it goes straight at the ingest cost Alex measured.
(e) RETIRE THE CODEGRAPH FOR COLLEAGUES: move them onto reflow2 views. Only possible once reflow2 renders something as readable as graphify's HTML and they choose to use it.

═══ COUNTER-ARGUMENTS, recorded beside the idea ═══
🛑 AGAINST (a), MEASURED ON REFLOW2 ITSELF: fact:adopt-ran-on-reflow2-and-the-mechanical-contract-recovery-collapsed. A mechanical scan produced 91 CONSUMES edges, 95 of 95 of them type references and not calls; the hand-authored sparse set was right and the dense mechanical one was wrong. Importing graphify's calls/imports as design edges would bury the real dependencies in coupling noise. dec:bl83a-functional-decomposition (accepted) also rules the design functional, not the file tree, so a component per module is the wrong altitude, and "the wrong altitude is harder to fix than an empty graph because it looks finished".
🛑 AGAINST (a), BY THE ONE-HOME RULE: code structure's home is the code. It is fully derivable from the repo at a commit. Storing it in the design makes a regenerable fact a hand-kept one that goes stale the moment the repo moves: a second source of truth of exactly the kind dec:idea-a-fact-has-one-home-across-a-family-of-designs-and-reflow2-enforces-it is against.
⚠️ SIZE: nine repos' codegraphs merged in would multiply the design's node count several times, most of it churn on every upstream commit.
⚠️ THE REAL SECOND SOURCE OF TRUTH IN hxm_program MAY BE A DIFFERENT FILE. The codegraph is generated. DECISIONS.md and planning/ are HAND-MAINTAINED beside 83 Decision nodes and the design's questions: that is where two records can actually disagree. fact:the-hub-hand-rolled-its-own-graph-tooling-per-repo-rather-than-waiting raised the same point on 2026-08-26 ("migration, rendering, or two records drifting apart").
⚠️ COLLEAGUES: whatever is chosen must leave the people who use the codegraph with something at least as good, or they keep using graphify and nothing is retired.

═══ SIZE, as information ═══
(b) is a stance, not a build. (c) is registering nine files, plus a node-id convention for the links. (d) is an adapter from graphify's JSON into adopt's structural phase. (e) depends on a reflow2 viewer that colleagues would adopt. (a) is a large import plus a lasting maintenance cost.
properties.name: SETTLED — promoted into: Adopt can take an existing code-structure graph (e.g. graphify's) as its mechanical pass: inventory, hashes and cycles by machine, intent by the agent (and 1 more)
properties.rationale: Homed in reflow2's design: whether reflow2 should hold, link or consume a code-structure graph is reflow2 behaviour; hxm_program is its first consumer, and it is only reachable here as files (not a connected child). Searched first with three read-path queries (graphify/codegraph/code-structure ingest; mechanical ingest; hub-built graph tooling) and read the three nearest in full: dec:idea-mechanical-code-structure-ingest, fact:the-hub-hand-rolled-its-own-graph-tooling-per-repo-rather-than-waiting and fact:adopt-ran-on-reflow2-and-the-mechanical-contract-recovery-collapsed. Also inspected hxm_program's codegraphs/build.sh and codegraphs/hextools/graph.json directly. Kept separate from dec:idea-mechanical-code-structure-ingest: that asks whether ADOPT should extract structure itself; this asks what becomes of an EXISTING code graph a program already maintains alongside its design, and whether the two can be one.
